newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM gets armoured car protection.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM gets armoured car protection.

text.p: Four armoured personnel carriers rolled through the Cambodian capital on Friday to beef up security at the house of co-Premier Hun Sen as political tension appeared to worsen after a deadly grenade attack.

Reuters reporters saw four armoured vehicles pass down a main boulevard, turn down the street where opposition leader Sam Rainsy's Khmer Nation Party (KNP) is headquartered, and pull into Hun Sen's compound.
Soldiers were on top of each armoured vehicle, and a pickup truck full of soldiers led the convoy. "They are there to protect Hun Sen," a soldier said.
The armoured personnel carriers sent jitters through the capital, which is still recovering from the shock of Sunday's grenade attack on a demonstration led by Sam Rainsy.
An Interior Ministry official from Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party (CPP) told Reuters security was being beefed up around Hun Sen's house on concern for his family's safety.
About 10 soldiers armed with machineguns were later seen in the southern part of the capital driving in the direction of a suburb where Hun Sen has another residence.
On Thursday, Hun Sen had said police were investigating two suspects over an alleged plot to assassinate members of his family, his friends and staff.
His comments came after four grenades ripped through the demonstration led by Sam Rainsy in the worst political violence in years, killing as many as 19 and wounding more than 100.

Sam Rainsy, who narrowly escaped injury, has accused Hun Sen of being behind the attack. Hun Sen has denied responsibility and condemned the violence but suggested that the protest leaders should be arrested.

A Western resident said it was possible the armoured personnel carriers were returning to the co-premier's house after providing security for Hun Sen in Oudong, an ancient capital of Cambodia 30 km (19 miles) north of Phnom Penh. The premier was attending religious ceremonies there on his birthday.
He said at least two of the armoured vehicles left the compound when Hun Sen was speaking near Oudong.
An interior ministry official played down the vehicle movements, saying the armoured carriers were usually stationed in the complex.
"The atmosphere is very tense," said Sam Rainsy, who said he had reports CPP officials were holding meetings and beefing up their military arsenals.
A human rights worker said tensions were unlikely to ease as local and national polls approached this year and next.

Hun Sen and co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh, who formed an uneasy coalition following U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993, have agreed on an investigation by the Interior Ministry into the grenade attack.
But Ranariddh, U.N. officials and parliamentarian Kem Sokha have expressed doubts that justice would be served by the ministry.
Hun Sen's CPP and Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party are expected to oppose each other in the elections.
